source: NASA/JPL (Voyager 2), public domain; Wikimedia Commons: Ariel (moon).jpg
originalProcessing: python3 scripts/compose-real-body.py <photo> content/icons/src/ariel.png round (turned so the sun is upper left, shaded with the sphere template at strength 1.4)
prompt: Precise restrained photo-based edit of ariel, a moon of Uranus. Preserve the existing photographed sunlit terrain, craters and canyon locations, orientation, grayscale color, circular globe size, and dominant NW upper-left key lighting. Change only the currently pitch-black lower-right hemisphere: complete its opaque spherical surface with very subtle inferred continuation of the cratered icy terrain and canyons, visible under weak neutral soft backlight/fill. The dark side must remain clearly much darker than the sunlit side, but not pure black, with a faint soft rim at the SE edge to define the complete circular body. No glowing neon outline, no atmosphere, no halo. House-style museum sphere lit from NW with weak reflected fill from SE. Do not replace visible photographed features with a different moon. Entire circle opaque, outside circle genuine transparency. Single full globe centered on square, 94% occupancy. No cast shadow, text, stars or background.

provenance.description: Voyager photo-based AI edit with subtle SE backlight and inferred dark-side terrain. Visible photographed geography guided the edit; added detail is not observed.

notes: House lighting: dominant NW key with weak neutral SE backlight/fill, so dark surfaces remain readable instead of completely black.
Backlight is restrained; no luminous halo or atmospheric glow.
Dark-side craters and canyons are artistic inference, not newly resolved Voyager observations.
